title: Peripherals: monitor, keyboard, mouse, printer and scanner

videos.script: The first two lessons were inside the box. This one is everything you actually touch. {{touch}} A peripheral is a translator. A keyboard turns a finger into a character. A mouse turns a movement into coordinates, and a scanner turns paper into pixels. A monitor and a printer run the same machinery backwards. {{translate}} That framing matters because it says where the failures are. Nothing here computes anything, so nothing here is slow the way a hard disk is slow. What goes wrong instead is a translation that is wrong, or expensive. A resolution the screen cannot really show. A keyboard that cannot type your own language without a fight. A printer whose ink costs more than the printer did. {{fail}} Two of those are paid for twice, and the last one is the largest single waste of money anywhere in this course. {{money}} We finish on two pictures you will be asked to put names on: the regions of a keyboard, and the inside of a scanner. You have looked at both for years without ever being told what the parts are called.
